title: Pope Leo calls for Yemen violence to end, in address two weeks after surgery
gist: Pope Leo, 71, appealed for an end to violence in Yemen, highlighting Taiz, in his first address two weeks after lung cancer surgery; he also condemned an attack on Orthodox faithful in Jordan.

themes.theme: Papal appeal on Yemen and Jordan

insights.claim: Pope Leo called for an end to hostilities in Yemen and expressed concern about the humanitarian situation in Taiz, where the population lacks food, water and medical assistance.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Elevates Yemen's humanitarian crisis in global attention.
insights.quote: where the population suffers due to the lack of food, water and medical assistance

insights.claim: The pope said he prays for victims of a 'terrorist attack against Orthodox faithful' at the Hamoud church in Jordan on Friday.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Signals sectarian-targeted violence in Jordan, normally seen as stable.

insights.claim: Pope Leo had the lower lobe of his right lung removed on October 13 after an adenocarcinoma diagnosis, and doctors said last week no further therapy is needed as the tumour had not spread.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Reduces near-term succession uncertainty at the Vatican.

insights.claim: The pope cancelled his planned attendance at a religious leaders' peace meeting in Assisi on Tuesday on doctors' advice.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Shows a cautious recovery; limited public schedule near-term.
